detail:
Key (NEW, UNSURE): R5|fnn-owner-response-window-close|direct-O @ host/native/owner.lisp:6113.

O is taken directly, outside the gate, and the function is not in direct_owner_sites (tools/lock_discipline_contracts.json). Callers: the mux loop (mux.lisp:398 via fnn-mux-cleanup-attempt, and :751) and the web actor (web-host.lisp:198). Added by 19ec62b71 (2026-10-03). A fault inside is routed to the fence (fnn-owner-thread-escape at mux.lisp:343). Open question: it calls fnn-owner-release-pending-extents-locked and fnn-owner-cold-window-result-locked; no read shows the cold-window result and pending-extent release are safe against the batch job, which runs off O, when entered ungated during an in-flight batch or a stop. Mux close must still run while stopping, so a gate refusal would be wrong.
fix: Either declare the function in direct_owner_sites with that proof (ordering against the off-O batch job and the stop path), or route it through fnn-section-run.
title: fnn-owner-response-window-close takes the owner mutex directly and is not a declared direct owner site (R5)
